title: Refresh tool calling docs + add known pitfalls + link runnable examples
author: Wei Chen
release_notes: Docs: Tool calling guide updated to match canonical semantics; added Known pitfalls section and linked runnable examples.
body:
## Summary
This updates our tool calling documentation to match the canonical cross-SDK semantics (as implemented in the refreshed examples) and adds a “Known pitfalls” section based on recent support + SE feedback.

Primary goals:
- Reduce copy/paste failures from outdated payload shapes.
- Make streaming + tool calls understandable across languages (esp. partial args + final assembly).
- Set expectations around parallel tool calls and safe handling of tool results.
- Point readers to runnable, maintained examples.

## What changed
- Rewrote the Tool calling guide to:
  - Use consistent terms: “tool definition”, “tool call”, “tool arguments”, “tool result message”.
  - Show the recommended message loop: user -> assistant (tool calls) -> tool result messages -> assistant (final).
  - Clarify when to validate arguments (before executing tools) and how to surface validation errors back to the model.
- Added a new “Known pitfalls (read this if things look flaky)” section covering:
  1) Partial tool arguments while streaming
     - Tool args may arrive as incremental deltas; do **not** JSON-parse until you have the final assembled args.
     - Recommendation: buffer tool_call.arguments text by tool_call_id, parse on completion, validate schema, then execute.
     - Explicit callout linked to SUP-18421 (truncated args mid-stream) and the workaround pattern.
  2) Parallel tool calls
     - Multiple tool calls can be requested in a single assistant turn; examples show iterating all tool calls and returning tool results for each.
     - Guidance: preserve tool_call_id, return results as separate tool messages, and avoid interleaving tool output with assistant text.
  3) Type/shape mismatches across languages
     - Added a short “shape” section explaining the stable fields we document and where SDKs differ in naming/typing.
     - Callout to SUP-18452 (TS type mismatch) and the updated TS example.
  4) Retry and failure handling
     - Guidance on tool execution failures (timeouts, non-200s): return a structured error payload as tool result, then allow the model to retry or choose a fallback.
     - Warning: do not silently drop tool failures; it produces confusing assistant behavior.
- Linked runnable examples:
  - Added “Try it now” links to redwood-examples streaming+tools sample (PR: redwood-examples#311) and referenced the quickstart template refresh (redwood-quickstarts#204) as a full app.
  - Added a short “Expected console output” block so readers know what success looks like.

## Files / pages touched (high level)
- docs/guides/tool-calling.mdx (major rewrite)
- docs/guides/streaming.mdx (small x-link + note about partial tool args)
- docs/reference/api/chat.mdx (terminology alignment + link to guide)
- docs/partials/known-pitfalls-tool-calling.mdx (new)
- sidebars + nav (moved tool calling to sit next to streaming + structured output)

## Screenshots
- N/A (content-only). Code tabs were verified manually.

## Test plan
- `pnpm install && pnpm build` (passes)
- `pnpm lint` (passes)
- `pnpm test:links` (passes)
- Manual:
  - Verified code tabs render for Python/TypeScript/Go and copy button works.
  - Clicked all new outbound links (examples + quickstarts) and ensured correct anchors.

## Notes for reviewers
- This PR intentionally avoids introducing new API semantics. It documents the canonical pattern already agreed in DevEx and implemented in the SDK/example refresh.
- If any page suggests we guarantee valid JSON in streamed tool arguments, please flag—this is explicitly not guaranteed.

## Review conversation highlights
- Elliot Price: Requested we move “Known pitfalls” higher on the page and add a one-sentence warning about parsing partial JSON during streaming. (Done)
- Ibrahim Khan: Asked for explicit guidance on buffering args by tool_call_id and parsing only on completion to prevent truncated-args bugs. (Added + linked SUP-18421)
- Brian Murphy: Requested a short, concrete parallel-tool example and clarification that tool results must be separate tool messages, not assistant text. (Added)
- Dana Lo: Requested TS wording change from “function call” to “tool call” and a note about runtime validation even with static types. (Updated)

## CI
All checks green:
- build
- lint
- typecheck
- link-check

Merged via squash to main.
